title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T — Dialysate Conductivity or Concentration Alarms
description: Troubleshooting guide for dialysate conductivity or concentration alarms on a Fresenius 2008T HD machine, focusing on external checks before escalation.

steps.title: Ensure the machine is safely powered down
steps.instructions: Disconnect the patient and stop any dialysis session. Power cycling the machine can sometimes clear false alarms.

steps.title: Check water source and connections
steps.instructions: Verify the water supply is on and free from leaks. Confirm all water inlet and return lines are securely connected. Dirty or partially blocked water lines can alter conductivity readings.

steps.title: Inspect concentrate supply
steps.instructions: Check that acid and bicarbonate concentrates are in the correct containers. Ensure containers are properly seated and the correct type is used. Confirm concentrates are not expired or contaminated.

steps.title: Examine dialysate lines and proportioning system
steps.instructions: Look for kinks, leaks, or disconnections in the dialysate delivery lines. Verify that proportioning lines from the concentrate containers are properly connected and unobstructed.

steps.title: Check conductivity sensor and calibration
steps.instructions: Wipe the sensor with a soft cloth if visibly dirty. Perform a conductivity calibration using manufacturer-provided calibration solution. Improper sensor readings are a common cause of concentration alarms.

steps.title: Review machine settings
steps.instructions: Confirm dialysate flow rate, target conductivity, and temperature settings are correct. Check for recent software updates or error logs that could indicate repeated sensor or calibration issues.

CCR.Complaint: Machine alarms for dialysate conductivity too low/high during setup.
CCR.Cause: Observed that the acid concentrate line was loosely connected and the conductivity sensor was dirty.
CCR.Resolution: Reconnected concentrate line and cleaned conductivity sensor. Calibrated sensor. Verified alarms cleared and machine passed self-test.

helpfulDetails: Water inlet pressure and filter status
Concentrate container type, volume, and expiration

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T — Blood Leak Detector Faults
description: This guide assists Clinical Engineering in troubleshooting blood leak detector faults on a Fresenius 2008T HD machine, focusing on external checks and patient safety.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient is not connected to the faulty machine. Move the patient to a standby or secondary machine if needed.

steps.title: Power and System Checks
steps.instructions: Verify the machine is powered on and not in an error state unrelated to the blood leak detector. Check that the machine is connected to a reliable power source; a low battery or unstable power can cause false faults.

steps.title: Inspect Blood Leak Sensor Area
steps.instructions: Check the dialyzer and bloodlines for proper installation. Misaligned blood leak sensors can trigger faults. Ensure the sensor clip is clean, dry, and free of residue or moisture that could interfere with detection.

steps.title: Check Bloodline Integrity
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, loose connections, or kinks in the bloodlines upstream of the sensor. Replace any damaged tubing.

steps.title: Inspect for Fluid Contamination
steps.instructions: Verify no saline or other fluids have entered the detector area; even small amounts can trigger a fault.

steps.title: Re-seat or Swap Sensor
steps.instructions: If the sensor appears physically intact but faults persist, remove and reseat it. If another identical sensor is available, swap to determine if the sensor itself is faulty.

steps.title: Review Machine Logs
steps.instructions: Check the 2008T’s event log for repeated blood leak alarms or unusual readings; patterns may indicate intermittent sensor failure or bloodline issue.

CCR.Complaint: Blood leak detector alarm triggered during treatment.
CCR.Cause: Sensor misalignment observed; bloodline properly installed, no visible leaks. Sensor shows intermittent readings even after cleaning and reseating.
CCR.Resolution: Re-seated sensor; replaced with a known-good sensor for testing. Machine continues to fault. Machine labeled Out of Service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Any abnormal alarm patterns or error codes recorded.
Final device status: Out of Service.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T — Air Detector Sensor Errors
description: Guide for troubleshooting air detector sensor errors on a Fresenius 2008T HD machine, emphasizing external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Verify Machine Power and Initialization
steps.instructions: Ensure the machine is plugged into a verified working outlet. Power the machine on and observe startup. A proper boot sequence ensures sensors are initializing correctly.

steps.title: Inspect Air Detector Sensor and Chamber
steps.instructions: Check the air detector chamber for cracks, cloudiness, or fluid buildup. Confirm the chamber is clean and correctly seated in its holder. Improper placement can trigger errors.

steps.title: Check Bloodline and Tubing Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure the arterial and venous bloodline tubing is correctly installed. Verify no kinks, bubbles, or disconnections exist upstream of the air detector. Even small bubbles can trigger a sensor alarm.

steps.title: Verify Sensor Calibration and Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the air detector sensor calibration status in the machine menu. If the calibration is overdue or fails, follow the manufacturer’s prompts to recalibrate.

steps.title: Check for Moisture or Condensation
steps.instructions: Moisture in or around the sensor can cause false readings. Dry the sensor area with a lint-free cloth if needed and restart the machine.

steps.title: Replace Disposable Components if Necessary
steps.instructions: If tubing or air detector chamber is suspected to be faulty, replace with new, manufacturer-approved components and retest.

steps.title: Observe Alarm Behavior During Test Run
steps.instructions: Run a priming or test cycle without a patient. Confirm that air detector readings are normal and no error alarms trigger.

CCR.Complaint: Air detector error alarm displayed during startup and/or treatment.
CCR.Cause: Observed misaligned or contaminated air detector chamber; tubing installed incorrectly; calibration overdue.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and reseated air detector chamber, verified tubing connections, recalibrated sensor, and ran a test cycle. If error persists, machine removed from service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (ready for use or removed from service)

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T — Ultrafiltration Control or Scale Calibration Issues
description: Guide to troubleshoot ultrafiltration control and scale calibration issues on Fresenius 2008T HD machines, emphasizing external causes before internal intervention.

steps.title: Verify the Machine Level and Placement
steps.instructions: Ensure the HD machine is on a stable, level surface. Ultrafiltration scales rely on level placement for accurate measurements. Why: Even slight tilting can cause erroneous readings.

steps.title: Check the Patient and Bloodline Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that all bloodlines, dialysate lines, and collection bags are properly seated. Ensure UF scales are unobstructed by floor mats, chairs, or other objects. Why: Misplacement can interfere with scale sensors and UF measurements.

steps.title: Inspect the UF Scale and Weight Sensors
steps.instructions: Visually check for debris, liquid spillage, or tubing pressing on the scale platform. Wipe the scale platform clean if necessary. Why: Physical interference can skew readings and cause alarms.

steps.title: Perform a UF Scale Calibration Check
steps.instructions: Follow the Fresenius 2008T prompts for “Scale Calibration” or “Weight Check” routine. Use known test weights if available. Why: Confirms that the scale sensor is functioning within acceptable parameters.

steps.title: Verify UF Settings in the Software
steps.instructions: Check prescribed UF rate and total UF target. Ensure machine software is not showing override messages or errors. Why: Incorrect programming can mimic scale or UF errors.

steps.title: Review Alarms or Event Logs
steps.instructions: Document any recent scale or UF alarms. Identify recurring patterns (e.g., certain shifts, room conditions, or patients). Why: Helps correlate errors with environmental or user-related factors.

CCR.Complaint: UF control is inaccurate, scale alarms triggered during dialysis session.
CCR.Cause: Scale platform was slightly obstructed by tubing and had minor liquid spillage; calibration check failed.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned scale platform, verified level placement, recalibrated scale; machine passed test and returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested for stability (to ensure power fluctuations are not affecting electronics)

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T — Blood Pump Motor or Flow Rate Failure
description: Troubleshooting guide for Clinical Engineering to address blood pump motor or flow rate failures on a Fresenius 2008T HD machine, emphasizing external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Verify Power and Machine Readiness
steps.instructions: Ensure the machine is properly connected to a verified power source. Confirm the machine has completed self-checks and displays no other critical errors. Why: Blood pump motors rely on stable voltage and startup sequences to function correctly.

steps.title: Inspect Blood Lines and Connections
steps.instructions: Check arterial and venous lines for kinks, clots, or air bubbles. Confirm all connectors are seated properly in the pump segment. Why: Obstructions or poor line placement can prevent the pump from reaching the set flow rate.

steps.title: Check Pump Segment Installation
steps.instructions: Verify the blood pump segment (cassette) is correctly installed and not worn or damaged. Look for wear, cracking, or misalignment that could affect flow. Why: Improper installation or worn segments can cause flow errors without motor failure.

steps.title: Assess Priming and Blood Flow Settings
steps.instructions: Ensure priming was completed successfully. Confirm the blood flow rate set on the machine is within safe operating limits. Why: High target flow rates or incomplete priming can trigger alarms or prevent the motor from achieving set speed.

steps.title: Observe Pump Operation During Test Mode
steps.instructions: If safe, run the pump in a test or maintenance mode without patient connection. Listen for unusual noises, vibration, or erratic rotation. Why: Motor noise or irregular movement can indicate mechanical failure or pump resistance.

steps.title: Check Machine Logs and Alarms
steps.instructions: Review error codes and event logs for indications of motor failure or flow restrictions. Why: Provides diagnostic insight without disassembly.

CCR.Complaint: Blood pump unable to reach prescribed flow rate; alarm triggered.
CCR.Cause: Pump segment properly installed; lines free of kinks; test run shows irregular pump rotation and motor noise.
CCR.Resolution: Machine removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent for vendor bench repair.

helpfulDetails: Blood line type and installation verified
Target and observed blood flow rate

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008 – Dialysate Conductivity or Mixing Alarms
description: Guide for troubleshooting dialysate conductivity or mixing alarms on Fresenius 5008 HD machines, focusing on external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Verify Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Ensure no patient is currently on the affected machine. If a patient is connected, move them to a standby or functioning HD machine before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Water Supply and Quality
steps.instructions: Confirm that the machine’s water inlet valves are fully open. Verify that RO water supply meets conductivity and purity specifications. Inspect for kinks, leaks, or blockages in the water inlet tubing.

steps.title: Inspect Concentrate Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure acid and bicarbonate concentrate lines are correctly connected and free of air bubbles. Check that concentrate bags are not expired or contaminated.

steps.title: Examine Dialysate Preparation and Flow
steps.instructions: Verify that the machine’s mixing chamber is free of residue or obstructions. Confirm that all valves related to dialysate mixing are operational and correctly seated.

steps.title: Check Conductivity Sensors
steps.instructions: Inspect the conductivity probe for fouling, residue, or misalignment. Clean the sensor according to Fresenius-approved procedures. Reinstall securely and retest calibration.

steps.title: Perform Machine Self-Check/Calibration
steps.instructions: Run the machine’s automatic dialysate conductivity calibration routine. Note any errors or failures during the procedure.

steps.title: Review Recent Maintenance or Changes
steps.instructions: Check if any recent service, part replacement, or water quality issues coincide with alarm onset. Document observations for troubleshooting history.

CCR.Complaint: Machine displays dialysate conductivity alarm intermittently during treatment.
CCR.Cause: Observed low dialysate conductivity due to air in concentrate lines and fouled conductivity sensor.
CCR.Resolution: Cleared air from lines, cleaned conductivity probe, ran calibration successfully, verified proper mixing. Machine returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Outlet tested and water quality confirmed.
Concentrate lines inspected and swapped if needed.
Final status: Machine operational and returning proper dialysate conductivity.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008 – Air Detector or Venous Pressure Sensor Faults
description: Guide for troubleshooting air detector or venous pressure sensor alarms on Fresenius 5008 HD machines, focusing on external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient is not actively connected to the machine before troubleshooting. Move the patient to another functional HD machine if necessary. Why: Air detection and venous pressure faults can trigger treatment interruptions or risk patient safety.

steps.title: Check Power and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the HD machine is plugged into a grounded outlet and properly powered on. Inspect sensor connectors for secure attachment. Why: Loose power or sensor connections can generate false alarms.

steps.title: Inspect Bloodlines and Tubing
steps.instructions: Examine arterial and venous bloodlines for kinks, clots, or air bubbles. Ensure all lines are seated properly in the sensor chambers. Why: Obstructions or air can falsely trigger sensor alarms.

steps.title: Clean Sensor Chambers
steps.instructions: For the air detector, check and clean the optical chamber if visibly dirty. For the venous pressure sensor, ensure the chamber is free from buildup or residue. Why: Contaminants can interfere with sensor readings.

steps.title: Run Self-Test or Calibration
steps.instructions: Use the machine’s built-in sensor test or calibration procedure for both air and venous pressure sensors. Document any errors during self-test. Why: Helps determine if the fault is reproducible or transient.

steps.title: Swap External Cables or Sensors (If Available)
steps.instructions: If a spare bloodline sensor assembly or cable exists, carefully swap to rule out faulty external components. Why: Isolates the fault to the sensor or machine electronics without disassembly.

CCR.Complaint: Machine shows repeated air detector or venous pressure alarms during treatment setup.
CCR.Cause: Bloodlines and connections inspected; no kinks or bubbles; optical chambers cleaned; self-test indicates persistent venous pressure sensor fault.
CCR.Resolution: Machine removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for service evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Any unusual sounds or indicator behavior

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008 – Blood Pump Speed or Motor Failure
description: Guide for troubleshooting abnormal blood pump speed readings or suspected motor failure on Fresenius 5008 HD machines, focusing on external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Stop dialysis and move the patient to another functioning machine. Confirm that the blood lines are clamped to prevent blood loss. Never troubleshoot the blood pump while the patient is connected.

steps.title: Verify Power Supply and Machine Startup
steps.instructions: Check that the machine is plugged into a verified working outlet. Inspect the main power cord and connector for damage. Restart the machine and monitor for normal startup sequence.

steps.title: Inspect Blood Lines and Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure bloodlines are properly installed without kinks or air bubbles. Confirm that the arterial and venous lines are not obstructed. Verify the transducer protector and tubing sensors are correctly seated.

steps.title: Check Blood Pump Settings and Alarms
steps.instructions: Review the prescribed blood flow rate; ensure it matches the prescription. Observe if the pump speed matches the displayed value. Listen for unusual noises indicating mechanical resistance or slipping.

steps.title: Verify Pump Motor Function with Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Use the machine’s built-in diagnostics menu to test the blood pump. Observe if the motor starts, reaches target RPM, and runs smoothly. Record any error codes displayed (e.g., motor drive, speed error).

steps.title: Inspect External Mechanical Components
steps.instructions: Check the roller head and pump segment for wear, debris, or misalignment. Ensure the pump segment rotates freely without obstruction. Replace pump tubing with a known good set if wear or cracking is present.

steps.title: Swap or Test Related Components (if available)
steps.instructions: Swap the pump tubing segment with a known functioning set to rule out tubing issues. If another compatible blood pump module exists, test the motor with it to isolate the fault.

CCR.Complaint: Blood pump not reaching prescribed speed; machine displays motor error.
CCR.Cause: Blood tubing and connections verified; pump segment rotates freely. Diagnostics indicate motor drive error.
CCR.Resolution: Machine removed from service, labeled “Out of Service,” and sent for bench evaluation or manufacturer repair.

helpfulDetails: Tubing checked for kinks or wear

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008 – Internal Fluid Leak Detection Alarms
description: Guide for troubleshooting internal fluid leak detection alarms on Fresenius 5008 HD machines, focusing on external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient is not actively on dialysis at the machine. Move the patient to a backup machine if necessary. Power down the unit before inspecting for leaks. Why: Prevents risk of electrical hazard or patient exposure to fluid contamination.

steps.title: Check Exterior for Visible Spills or Moisture
steps.instructions: Inspect around the bloodlines, dialyzer, and dialysate connections. Wipe up any accidental spills and ensure tubing is routed correctly. Why: External fluid can trigger internal sensors if it seeps into the machine casing.

steps.title: Verify All Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm all dialysate, blood, and effluent lines are properly seated and not cracked or leaking. Check clamps and connectors for tightness. Why: Loose or cracked lines can drip into the machine and trigger alarms.

steps.title: Inspect Drain and Waste Systems
steps.instructions: Ensure the drain hose is correctly positioned and free of kinks. Confirm the drain pan or bottle is not overfilled. Why: Backflow or overflow can simulate an internal leak.

steps.title: Check Internal Sensor Area for Contamination
steps.instructions: Open the machine panel only if the manufacturer guidance allows, carefully inspect the fluid detection sensor area for residue or moisture. Use a dry cloth to remove any detected moisture. Why: Residual fluid can falsely trigger alarms.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Machine
steps.instructions: Turn off the machine, wait 30–60 seconds, and power it back on. Observe whether the alarm reoccurs without connecting a patient. Why: Confirms whether the alarm is persistent (possible internal leak) or transient (external contamination).

CCR.Complaint: Internal fluid leak alarm triggered during machine startup.
CCR.Cause: No external leaks observed; internal sensor area inspected and cleaned; alarm persisted after power cycle.
CCR.Resolution: Machine removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for bench evaluation/repair.

helpfulDetails: Machine serial number and last service date.
Any unusual odors or moisture inside the machine.
Alarm codes displayed on the screen.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008 – User Interface or Touchscreen Communication Faults
description: Guide for troubleshooting user interface or touchscreen communication faults on Fresenius 5008 hemodialysis machines, focusing on external causes and safe escalation.

steps.title: Verify Power Supply
steps.instructions: Ensure the machine is plugged into a functioning, grounded outlet. Confirm that the main power switch is ON. Observe any power indicators on the display. Why: Unstable or missing power can cause touchscreen and interface faults.

steps.title: Inspect Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: Check the connection between the touchscreen and the main control unit. Ensure cables are firmly seated and not damaged. Why: Loose or damaged cables can disrupt communication between the touchscreen and CPU.

steps.title: Check for External Interference
steps.instructions: Ensure no strong electromagnetic devices (like cell phones or other medical devices) are near the machine. Why: Electromagnetic interference can cause intermittent UI issues.

steps.title: Perform a Soft Reboot
steps.instructions: Power cycle the machine using the standard shutdown and startup procedure. Monitor the UI response during startup. Why: Temporary software glitches can often be resolved by restarting.

steps.title: Check for Visible Screen Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen for cracks, scratches, or liquid ingress. Ensure the screen is clean and dry. Why: Physical damage or contamination can prevent proper touch detection.

steps.title: Observe Software Messages
steps.instructions: Note any error codes or messages displayed on the UI. Record exact wording for documentation. Why: Error codes can indicate specific communication faults or sensor failures.

steps.title: Swap with Known Good User Interface (if available)
steps.instructions: If your department maintains spare touchscreens, carefully replace and test. Why: Confirms whether the issue is the touchscreen or another internal component.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen unresponsive; unable to navigate menus.
CCR.Cause: Power verified; cables secure; no visible damage; soft reboot did not resolve; UI remains unresponsive.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, escalated to vendor for repair.

helpfulDetails: Touchscreen condition inspected (clean, dry, no visible damage)

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Alarm: Fill Program Alarm
description: Troubleshooting a Fill Program Alarm caused by persistent detected air or incomplete dialysate filling while blood is sensed, preventing normal completion of the filling program.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Fill Program Alarm occurs during treatment, notify clinical staff immediately and ensure safe alternate dialysis support according to clinical protocol. Remove the affected 2008T from patient use before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Alarm and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the status box displays Fill Program Alarm. Document when the alarm occurs, whether blood was sensed, whether visible air or abnormal fluid level is present, and whether related flow or hydraulic indications are reported.

steps.title: Check the Air Separation Chamber for Persistent Air
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, inspect the accessible air separation chamber for persistent visible air, abnormal fluid level, failure to clear air, obvious leaks, loose fittings, or damaged tubing.

steps.title: Inspect External Fluid Connections and Setup Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm external fluid lines are correctly installed and secure. Inspect accessible tubing and connections for kinks, looseness, cracks, damage, leakage, contamination, or possible air entry. Review whether the complaint began after setup, disinfection, transport, or accessory change.

steps.title: Evaluate Accessible Air-Sensing Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible sensing area for contamination, moisture, residue, obstruction, component misalignment, or obvious connector damage. Do not perform invasive internal repair during initial troubleshooting.

steps.title: Observe for Continued Abnormal Fill or Flow Behavior
steps.instructions: With the machine out of patient use, observe whether the filling program completes normally and document any repeated alarm recurrence, continued air-clearing failure, abnormal draining behavior, or related hydraulic alarms.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, verify that the filling program completes normally, confirm the alarm does not recur during approved functional testing, complete required safety checks, and document the final device status.

CCR.Complaint: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T displayed Fill Program Alarm during treatment with blood sensed and remained in the filling program beyond 60 seconds.
CCR.Cause: Persistent air-related fill condition observed. External tubing and accessible connections were checked with no correctable external cause identified; alarm persisted during out-of-service testing.
CCR.Resolution: Machine removed from patient use, labeled Out of Service, and routed for bench evaluation of the air-sensing path, valve 43 function, and related hydraulic operation.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Alarm: NO WATER
description: Troubleshooting the No Water alarm when inadequate inlet water supply or failed level detection interrupts normal hydraulic operation and causes heater shutdown.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the No Water alarm occurs during dialysis, notify clinical staff immediately and ensure the patient receives safe alternate dialysis support or appropriate clinical intervention. Remove the affected 2008T from patient use until the cause is identified and normal operation is verified.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Alarm and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the status box displays No Water. Document whether the alarm occurs during startup, rinse, treatment preparation, treatment, or intermittently, and note associated heater shutdown or interrupted hydraulic operation.

steps.title: Check the Incoming Water Source
steps.instructions: Verify the water supply is on and available. Check for a closed supply valve, disconnected connection, restricted line, facility water interruption, or RO distribution problem. Verify incoming water pressure is within 20 to 105 PSI when appropriate.

steps.title: Check Incoming Water Temperature
steps.instructions: Confirm incoming water temperature is within 10°C to 25°C. Correct any out-of-specification supply condition before continuing device evaluation.

steps.title: Inspect the Water Inlet Tubing and Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect external inlet tubing for kinks, crushing, leaks, loose connections, obstruction, or incorrect routing. Correct any external tubing issue and retest the machine.

steps.title: Inspect the Inlet Filter Screen
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible inlet filter screen for contamination, debris, or blockage according to approved service practice. Clean or replace only as permitted, then retest.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Problem Follows the Water Supply or the Device
steps.instructions: When safe and permitted, compare operation using a known-working dialysis machine on the same approved water source or evaluate the affected machine on a verified acceptable source.

steps.title: Evaluate the Water Inlet Regulator and Valve 41 Function
steps.instructions: If external supply conditions are acceptable but the alarm persists, assess whether the inlet regulator or valve 41 is preventing adequate water entry when water is requested. Perform internal evaluation only if authorized and trained.

steps.title: Assess Float-Switch or Level-Sensing Function
steps.instructions: If adequate water is reaching the inlet path but the No Water alarm remains, evaluate the float switch or associated level-sensing function according to approved service procedure.

steps.title: Confirm Resolution Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: Operate the machine through appropriate operational checks away from patient use. Confirm the alarm does not recur, water supply remains stable, no leakage is present, normal operation is restored, and required verification is completed before return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Fresenius 2008T displayed No Water alarm during startup. Machine did not detect rising inlet water level and could not proceed with normal water-dependent operation.
CCR.Cause: Incoming water tubing was found kinked behind the machine, restricting inlet flow and preventing adequate water level rise after inlet valve 41 was commanded open.
CCR.Resolution: Removed machine from clinical availability, corrected the kinked inlet water tubing, verified acceptable water supply, completed operational testing, and confirmed the No Water alarm did not recur. Unit returned to service.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Error: Flow Inlet Error
description: Troubleshooting Flow Inlet Error when the expected low hydrochamber level is not detected after balancing chamber cycling, interrupting hydraulic operation and disabling the heater.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the error occurs during dialysis treatment, notify clinical staff immediately and manage treatment using approved clinical procedures and alternate dialysis support as appropriate. Never troubleshoot while the affected machine is being relied upon for active patient treatment.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the machine removed from patient use, confirm that Flow Inlet Error is displayed. Document whether it occurs during startup, setup, or operation; whether it appears immediately after balancing chamber cycling; whether it is intermittent or repeatable; whether the machine was outside recirculation; and whether heater shutdown or abnormal hydraulic behavior occurs.

steps.title: Check the External Water Supply and Inlet Path
steps.instructions: Verify that the facility water source is available and stable, the water supply connection is secure, and the inlet tubing is free of kinks, pinching, collapse, leaks, visible restriction, contamination, or obstruction. Correct obvious external concerns and retest.

steps.title: Inspect the Hydrochamber Level Condition
steps.instructions: Observe hydrochamber level behavior during permitted Clinical Engineering evaluation. Look for a level that does not change as expected, remains high when a low condition should be detected, contains unusual bubbles or contamination, or shows signs that the float is not responding freely.

steps.title: Evaluate the Float-Switch and Level-Sensing Response
steps.instructions: Compare actual hydrochamber level movement with the machine response. If the level visibly changes but the error remains, suspect a float-switch or sensing concern. If the level does not change, continue isolating an inlet-flow, valve, or hydraulic-path concern. Inspect accessible sensing-related connections for obvious defects.

steps.title: Check Accessible Inlet Water Valve Conditions
steps.instructions: Evaluate whether the accessible inlet water path supports normal hydrochamber filling and level transition. Inspect for evidence of restricted flow, leakage, abnormal response, obstruction, or incorrect accessible tubing connections.

steps.title: Assess the Error Pattern During Balancing Chamber Cycling
steps.instructions: Determine whether the error consistently appears immediately after balancing chamber cycles and whether hydraulic flow appears abnormal during the cycle. Document findings suggesting valve malfunction, improper flow transition, or likely internal hydraulic failure. Do not perform internal hydraulic disassembly during external troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm Resolution Before Returning the Machine to Service
steps.instructions: After correcting any external water supply, tubing, obstruction, or accessible connection issue, operate the machine through the condition that previously produced the error. Confirm that Flow Inlet Error no longer appears, hydrochamber level changes are detected normally, heater shutdown does not recur, no additional hydraulic alarms occur, and required operational and safety checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T displayed Flow Inlet Error during operation after balancing chamber cycling. Heater shut off and machine did not detect the expected low hydrochamber level condition.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found restricted inlet water tubing preventing normal hydrochamber level change after balancing chamber cycling.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected inlet tubing restriction, verified secure water inlet connection, and tested machine through repeated operating cycles. Flow Inlet Error did not recur; device passed operational verification and was returned to service.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Error: Flow Error
description: Troubleshooting Flow Error when balancing chamber switching does not occur within the expected time, interrupting dialysate flow operation and turning the heater off.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If Flow Error occurs during treatment, notify clinical staff immediately, move the patient to safe alternate dialysis support as clinically appropriate, and remove the affected machine from patient use before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Associated Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that Flow Error is displayed while the machine is out of patient use. Document whether it occurs during startup, rinse, preparation, or operating flow; whether it is repeatable; whether dialysate flow is interrupted; whether the heater turns off; and whether additional alarms, leaks, or abnormal sounds are present.

steps.title: Check Power, Operating State, and Visible Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm normal power-up behavior and verify that the machine is in a state where dialysate flow is expected rather than flow-off or no-program mode. Inspect accessible areas for leaks, moisture, visible contamination, unusual pump sounds, or absent expected hydraulic activity.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible Dialysate Flow Path and Connections
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible tubing and connections for kinks, pinching, collapse, disconnection, incorrect routing, visible obstruction, residue, or leakage. Correct only clearly external and accessible issues before retesting.

steps.title: Observe for Evidence of Flow Pump Operation
steps.instructions: During an out-of-service functional check, observe whether expected pump activity occurs when flow is commanded. Note stalling, grinding, intermittent operation, repeated unsuccessful attempts, or whether the error appears after an attempt to establish flow. Do not disassemble hydraulic assemblies.

steps.title: Evaluate Balancing Chamber Switching Behavior
steps.instructions: Observe whether balancing chamber cycling appears to begin before Flow Error occurs. Document abnormal or missing valve-actuation sounds, repeated unsuccessful cycling, flow that begins and stops, or recurrence at the same operating point.

steps.title: Correct External Issues and Retest Out of Patient Use
steps.instructions: If an accessible tubing restriction, loose connection, leak, or setup concern is corrected, retest according to facility procedure. Confirm normal flow sequence, no recurrence of Flow Error, no associated leaks or alarms, and successful operational verification.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the machine to service only when normal dialysate flow operation is verified, the heater remains available as expected, Flow Error does not recur, and all facility requirements for safe return to use are met.

CCR.Complaint: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T displayed Flow Error during dialysate flow operation and the heater turned off when the error occurred.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed recurring Flow Error after checking accessible tubing, connections, visible leak conditions, and operating setup. No external restriction identified; condition indicates likely internal balancing chamber switching, pressure sensing, valve, flow pump, or hydraulic control fault.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from service and labeled Out of Service for bench evaluation of dialysate flow, balancing chamber operation, chamber full sensing, and associated hydraulic components. Device not returned to clinical use pending repair and verification.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 2008T Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Error: High Flow Error
description: Troubleshooting High Flow Error when abnormally rapid balancing chamber switching causes heater shutdown and may prevent dependable dialysis operation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If High Flow Error occurs during treatment, notify clinical staff immediately and ensure safe alternate dialysis support or appropriate clinical intervention before removing the affected machine from patient use.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that High Flow Error appears on the display, document when it occurs, observe whether it is continuous or intermittent, confirm whether heater shutdown occurs, and record the selected dialysate flow setting.

steps.title: Check the Selected Flow Setting and Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that the selected dialysate flow rate is appropriate for the intended test or operating condition and confirm that no unintended setting or unusual setup condition is contributing to rapid balancing chamber cycling.

steps.title: Inspect External Dialysate and Hydraulic Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible external tubing and connections for correct routing, secure connection, kinks, collapse, damage, leakage, contamination, loose fittings, bypassed routing, or external accessories altering normal flow behavior.

steps.title: Restart and Observe Error Recurrence
steps.instructions: With the machine out of patient use, rerun the applicable preparation or test sequence according to facility procedure and observe whether High Flow Error returns, whether it is flow-setting dependent, and whether heater shutdown recurs.

steps.title: Identify the Likely Failure Category
steps.instructions: If setup and external checks are normal, suspect an internal condition involving flow-pump operation, chamber full switch signal, balancing chamber cycling, valve operation, or hydraulic flow-control function and escalate for qualified evaluation.

steps.title: Verify Resolution Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: If an external or configuration issue is corrected, complete applicable operational verification, confirm that High Flow Error does not recur, and document the corrective action and final device status before return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Fresenius 2008T displayed High Flow Error during preparation or operational testing, with heater shutdown observed when the condition occurred.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed selected dialysate flow setting and inspected accessible external hydraulic tubing and connections. High Flow Error remained reproducible, indicating suspected internal flow-pump, chamber full switch, balancing chamber, valve, or hydraulic flow-control malfunction.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from service and labeled Out of Service for qualified bench evaluation and repair. Unit not returned to patient use pending successful operational verification.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Arterial or Venous Pressure Reading Is Incorrect
description: Use this guide when arterial or venous pressure appears inaccurate, unstable, absent, or inconsistent due to tubing, transducer interfaces, setup, or sensing faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unreliable Pressure Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment when arterial or venous pressure monitoring is unreliable and the cause cannot be immediately identified. Move the patient to another verified machine when necessary before technical troubleshooting. Do not defeat pressure alarms or alter limits to conceal an abnormal reading. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on unreliable pressure monitoring.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Reading Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the arterial pressure, venous pressure, or both are affected. Establish whether the reading is absent, fixed, fluctuating, offset, or simply inconsistent with the clinical situation. Record the displayed values and any associated alarm message. Expected outcome: The specific measurement problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Bloodline and Pressure Tubing
steps.instructions: With the machine out of patient use, inspect the applicable pressure line and bloodline for kinks, clamps, occlusions, loose fittings, leaks, fluid intrusion, collapsed tubing, or incorrect routing. Expected outcome: Tubing and pressure pathways are correctly routed, open where intended, and securely connected.

steps.title: 4. Check the Pressure Interface
steps.instructions: Inspect the external pressure connection or interface for proper seating and physical damage. Confirm the applicable line is fully connected and not partially detached. Do not access or adjust internal pressure sensors. Expected outcome: The external pressure interface is correctly assembled. If reconnecting it restores a plausible stable reading, continue to verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Disposable Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm the approved disposable bloodline set is installed correctly and that pressure monitoring components are in their intended positions. Compare with a properly configured known-good machine if uncertainty exists. Expected outcome: Disposable setup matches normal configuration and no installation error is present.

steps.title: 6. Replace Questionable External Components
steps.instructions: When appropriate, repeat testing with a known-good compatible bloodline or pressure monitoring component. Do not reuse components suspected of leakage, contamination, or deformation. Expected outcome: The problem either follows the disposable component or remains with the machine. If a known-good component restores normal pressure measurement, replace the affected disposable and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Mechanical Causes During Simulated Operation
steps.instructions: Using an approved nonpatient test setup, observe whether the reading responds logically to expected changes in the circuit. Ensure clamps, pumps, tubing, and circuit routing are not creating an artificial pressure condition. Expected outcome: Pressure readings respond in a stable and plausible manner to changes in the test setup.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the arterial and venous pressure channels display stable, plausible values and associated alarms or protective responses function as required by approved testing. Do not return the device to clinical service if a pressure channel intermittently freezes, drifts, or behaves unpredictably. Expected outcome: Both pressure measurements operate consistently through final testing. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the venous pressure reading on the 5008S CorDiax was intermittently low and unstable during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external pressure line connection was loose and intermittently venting.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was secured, pressure response was verified with a nonpatient functional test, and the machine was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Arterial, venous, or both channels affected.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Leak or Air Detector Alarm Repeats
description: Use this guide for repeated blood leak or air detector alarms caused by disposables, bubbles, positioning, contamination, connections, or detector-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Treat the Alarm as Real
steps.instructions: Do not assume a repeated blood leak or air detector alarm is false. Follow the clinical response appropriate to the alarm and ensure the patient is not dependent on a system whose protective detection function is unreliable. Move the patient to another verified device when needed before Clinical Engineering troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient safety is maintained and the affected machine can be evaluated without bypassing a protective alarm.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Detector Is Alarming
steps.instructions: Determine whether the report involves the blood leak detector, air detector, or both. Record the exact displayed message and when the alarm occurs. Ask whether the alarm began after setup, a disposable change, repositioning, or an actual visible bubble or fluid abnormality. Expected outcome: The specific detector and operating condition associated with the alarm are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Extracorporeal Circuit and Disposables
steps.instructions: Check the installed tubing and disposable components for correct routing, complete seating, kinks, damaged segments, visible air, loose connections, inappropriate fluid level, or obvious leakage. Do not manipulate a patient-connected circuit solely for technical troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The external circuit is correctly installed and free of obvious conditions capable of generating a legitimate alarm.

steps.title: 4. Verify Detector-Specific Positioning
steps.instructions: Inspect the tubing or chamber where it passes through the applicable detector. Confirm it is fully seated, correctly positioned, and not twisted, stretched, contaminated, or partially outside the sensing area. Expected outcome: The disposable is positioned correctly within the detector. If reseating corrects the alarm and it does not recur during verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Look for Air or Foam
steps.instructions: Check for residual air, foam, or repeated bubble formation in the circuit during a nonpatient test setup. Determine whether an upstream connection, poorly seated disposable, or inadequate priming condition is contributing. Expected outcome: No persistent air or foam enters the monitored section. If correcting the external cause eliminates the alarm, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Blood Leak Detection Area
steps.instructions: For blood leak complaints, inspect accessible detector surfaces and the dialysate path interface for visible contamination or residue according to approved cleaning practices. Do not open internal optical assemblies or alter detector alignment. Expected outcome: Accessible sensing surfaces are clean and unobstructed. If approved cleaning resolves the repeated alarm, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Approved Known-Good Disposables
steps.instructions: When appropriate, repeat the test with a verified compatible disposable set to determine whether the problem follows the tubing, chamber, or other external component. Expected outcome: The alarm either follows an external disposable or remains with the machine. If a known-good disposable eliminates the problem, replace the defective disposable and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Protective Alarm Function
steps.instructions: After correcting any external cause, perform the applicable approved operational checks to confirm the detector is recognized and the machine operates normally without nuisance alarms. Do not attempt to defeat, desensitize, or adjust protective detection functions outside authorized procedures. Expected outcome: No unexplained alarm recurs and the applicable protective function passes required verification.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported repeated air detector alarms during setup on the 5008S CorDiax.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the tubing segment was not fully seated in the air detector and was partially outside the sensing area.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was correctly positioned, a nonpatient functional check was completed without recurrent alarms, and the machine was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Blood leak versus air detector alarm.
Stage of setup or treatment when alarm occurs.
Visible air, foam, blood, or contamination.
Disposable lot or type if relevant.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Blood Pump Will Not Run or Speed Is Unstable
description: Use this guide when the blood pump does not start, stops unexpectedly, or runs inconsistently because of tubing, interlocks, settings, loading, or drive faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Blood-Circuit Safety
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable blood pump while a patient depends on it for active treatment. Follow the clinical contingency process and move treatment to a verified machine when required. Prevent unintended blood movement while inspecting the pump area. Expected outcome: The patient and extracorporeal circuit are safely managed before technical troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pump Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the blood pump does not start, starts and stops, runs at the wrong apparent speed, produces abnormal noise, or becomes unstable only at certain times. Record any displayed message or interlock indication. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined and distinguished from a commanded pump stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Operating Conditions and Commands
steps.instructions: Check that the machine is in a state that permits blood-pump operation and that the requested operator setting has been entered correctly. Confirm no active safety alarm or interlock is intentionally preventing pump operation. Expected outcome: The pump is being commanded to run under conditions where operation should be permitted. If clearing a legitimate setup condition restores normal operation, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Bloodline Loading
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the circuit, inspect the pump tubing segment for correct loading, seating, orientation, tension, and closure of the accessible pump mechanism. Look for twisted, stretched, flattened, damaged, or incorrectly sized tubing. Expected outcome: The tubing segment is correctly installed and can move freely through the pump mechanism.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Pump Area for Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check accessible surfaces for foreign material, dried residue, displaced tubing, or another external obstruction that could interfere with rotation or closure. Do not disassemble the pump drive or defeat protective covers or interlocks. Expected outcome: The pump path is clear and accessible mechanical parts move only as intended.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Disposable Set
steps.instructions: If tubing condition is questionable, use an approved known-good disposable set for a nonpatient test. Observe whether the pump starts and maintains commanded operation. Expected outcome: If the pump operates normally with a known-good disposable, the original tubing or installation was the likely cause and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Observe Pump Operation Without Patient Use
steps.instructions: Run the machine under an approved nonpatient test condition and observe for hesitation, speed fluctuation, unusual sound, vibration, or intermittent stopping. Do not continue operating the pump if abnormal mechanical noise or binding occurs. Expected outcome: The pump operates smoothly and consistently at the commanded setting.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify normal blood-pump startup, stop, control response, and stable operation through the applicable checks. Confirm no related alarms recur. Expected outcome: Pump operation is smooth and consistent and all applicable protective functions remain intact. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the blood pump on the 5008S CorDiax would start and then stop during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the pump tubing segment was twisted and not fully seated in the pump path.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was correctly reloaded, pump operation remained stable through nonpatient functional testing, and the machine was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Pump does not start versus unstable speed.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Concentrate, Solution, or Disposable Is Not Detected
description: Use this guide when the machine does not recognize a required concentrate, solution, connector, or disposable because of setup, seating, identification, or interface problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Do Not Bypass Recognition Checks
steps.instructions: Do not begin or continue treatment when a required concentrate, solution, or disposable is not recognized. Move the patient to a verified machine if the condition cannot be promptly corrected before treatment. Do not bypass recognition or safety interlocks. Expected outcome: Treatment does not proceed with an unverified fluid or disposable setup.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Is Not Being Detected
steps.instructions: Identify the specific concentrate, solution, connector, disposable, or related component named by the machine. Record the exact displayed message and whether the issue occurs every time or only with one item. Expected outcome: The affected item and recognition point are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Item Is Installed
steps.instructions: Confirm the component is approved for the 5008S CorDiax and appropriate for the intended treatment setup. Check labeling, packaging, condition, and obvious compatibility. Expected outcome: The correct item is being used. If the wrong component is found, replace it with the correct item and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Seating and Connection
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the item when safe, ensuring connectors, holders, caps, pickup points, and other accessible interfaces are fully seated. Inspect for bent, damaged, wet, dirty, or obstructed external connection surfaces. Expected outcome: The item is fully and correctly installed. If recognition returns and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Item for Damage
steps.instructions: Check the disposable, container, connector, or solution interface for cracks, deformation, damaged identification features, leakage, contamination, or packaging damage. Do not attempt to modify a disposable to make it detectable. Expected outcome: The installed item is physically intact and suitable for use.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Approved Item
steps.instructions: Replace the questionable component with a verified compatible item. If the problem follows the original item, remove that item from use according to facility practice. Expected outcome: If a known-good item is detected normally, the original item or its setup was the cause and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Accessible Recognition Area
steps.instructions: Check the applicable accessible machine interface for residue, fluid, foreign material, or obvious physical damage. Clean only according to approved procedures. Do not open the recognition assembly or alter internal sensors. Expected outcome: The external recognition area is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine consistently recognizes the required concentrate, solution, or disposable through normal setup and preparation without recurrent messages. Expected outcome: Recognition remains stable and normal preparation can proceed. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the 5008S CorDiax would not recognize the installed concentrate connection during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the concentrate connector was not fully seated in the machine interface.
CCR.Resolution: The connector was correctly installed, recognition remained normal through preparation, and the machine was returned to service after functional verification.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Conductivity Will Not Stabilize or Is Out of Range
description: Use this guide for unstable or unacceptable dialysate conductivity caused by concentrate supply, connections, preparation, water supply, setup, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Unreliable Dialysate Delivery
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment when dialysate conductivity cannot be verified as acceptable. If the condition occurs during treatment, follow the clinical procedure for maintaining patient safety and transfer to another verified machine when required. Do not bypass conductivity monitoring or defeat protective alarms. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer dependent on a machine with questionable dialysate composition. Troubleshooting can proceed safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether conductivity fails to stabilize during preparation, changes intermittently, remains consistently high or low, or becomes abnormal only after treatment begins. Record the displayed condition and any associated messages before changing the setup. Expected outcome: The exact pattern is documented and distinguished from a one-time setup error.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Concentrates Are Present
steps.instructions: Confirm the prescribed and facility-approved concentrate products are being used and that containers are correctly identified, adequately filled, and not visibly contaminated or damaged. Check that acid and bicarbonate sources have not been swapped, mixed incorrectly, or connected to the wrong pickup path. Expected outcome: Correct concentrate sources are available and properly identified. If an incorrect concentrate setup is found and correcting it restores stable conductivity, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Concentrate Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible concentrate connectors, pickup tubes, caps, hoses, and interfaces for looseness, kinks, cracks, blocked openings, air entry, or incomplete insertion. Reseat accessible connections as appropriate without opening internal fluid pathways. Expected outcome: Concentrate connections are secure and capable of supplying fluid without visible restriction or air entry.

steps.title: 5. Check Concentrate Supply and Pickup
steps.instructions: Confirm pickup tubing is actually immersed in the intended solution and is not resting above the fluid level, pressed against a container wall, kinked, or drawing visible air. If allowed by facility practice, replace a questionable concentrate container with a verified known-good container of the correct product. Expected outcome: The machine has a continuous external concentrate supply. If conductivity stabilizes after correcting the supply, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Water Supply Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine has an adequate, stable water connection and that the supply hose is not kinked, leaking, disconnected, or affected by an obvious facility water issue. Compare with nearby dialysis machines when appropriate to determine whether multiple machines are experiencing the same problem. Expected outcome: A machine-specific versus facility-wide water problem is identified. If multiple units are affected, escalate the water or infrastructure issue rather than assuming an individual machine failure.

steps.title: 7. Check Setup and Operating Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify the treatment or preparation setup has not been entered incorrectly and that the selected concentrate configuration matches the intended clinical setup. Do not make unauthorized configuration or service-menu changes to force conductivity into range. Expected outcome: User-accessible settings and concentrate selections agree with the intended setup.

steps.title: 8. Use Known-Good External Supplies
steps.instructions: When permitted, repeat preparation using known-good approved concentrate containers and normal water supply conditions. Observe whether conductivity stabilizes without repeated fluctuation. Expected outcome: The fault either follows an external supply item or remains with the machine. If known-good supplies correct the condition, replace the defective or incorrect external supply and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Allow the machine to complete its normal preparation and verify conductivity remains stable through the required operational checks without recurrent alarms. Do not return a machine to service based on a brief momentary normal reading after repeated instability. Expected outcome: Conductivity remains stable throughout the required verification period and no related alarms recur. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported conductivity would not stabilize during preparation on the 5008S CorDiax.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the concentrate pickup connection was not fully seated and was intermittently drawing air.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was properly seated, preparation was repeated, conductivity remained stable through functional verification, and the machine was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether conductivity was high, low, or unstable.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Dialysate Temperature Is High, Low, or Unstable
description: Use this guide when dialysate temperature is high, low, or fluctuating due to setup, supply, environment, flow, or service-level temperature-control problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unverified Dialysate Temperature
steps.instructions: Do not continue treatment when dialysate temperature is unreliable or repeatedly alarming. Move the patient to another verified machine as clinically appropriate before technical troubleshooting. Do not bypass or silence a protective temperature condition to maintain treatment. Expected outcome: The affected machine is no longer relied upon for patient treatment until temperature control is verified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Temperature Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the temperature remains too high, remains too low, fluctuates, or fails only during a particular stage of preparation or treatment. Record the displayed value or message and whether the condition begins immediately or after the machine has been operating. Expected outcome: The temperature problem is clearly characterized and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Selected Temperature Setting
steps.instructions: Check the normal operator-accessible treatment settings and confirm the intended dialysate temperature has been selected. Compare against the treatment prescription or a known-good machine when appropriate. Expected outcome: The selected setting matches the intended clinical setup. If the wrong setting caused the condition and correction restores normal operation, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Verify Water Supply and External Flow Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect the incoming water connection for kinks, restriction, leakage, or obvious interruption. Confirm that the facility supply is available and that nearby machines are not showing similar temperature or water-related problems. Expected outcome: The machine has a stable external water supply and any facility-wide issue is identified.

steps.title: 5. Check the Operating Environment
steps.instructions: Ensure ventilation openings are clear and that the machine is not positioned against a heat source, in direct sunlight, or in an unusually cold or hot environment. Inspect for excessive external heat around the machine or signs of blocked airflow. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions are not contributing to unstable thermal performance.

steps.title: 6. Allow Normal Stabilization
steps.instructions: With the machine out of patient use, restart preparation under normal conditions and observe whether temperature stabilizes as the machine completes its usual preparation cycle. Avoid repeated rapid restarts or attempts to force operation through persistent temperature alarms. Expected outcome: Temperature stabilizes and remains controlled through normal preparation. If it does, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Machine
steps.instructions: When practical, compare the same water source, room conditions, and operating setup with another functioning dialysis machine. If the comparison machine behaves normally while the 5008S CorDiax remains unstable, a machine-specific problem becomes more likely. Expected outcome: External environmental and infrastructure causes are either identified or reasonably ruled out.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the machine maintains stable temperature throughout the applicable preparation and operational checks and that no temperature-related alarms recur. If temperature again drifts or alarms, remove the machine from service. Expected outcome: Dialysate temperature remains stable during verification. If successful, troubleshooting can stop and normal return-to-service processes may proceed.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the 5008S CorDiax dialysate temperature fluctuated during machine preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the incoming water hose partially kinked behind the machine, restricting normal supply conditions.
CCR.Resolution: The hose was repositioned, preparation was repeated, temperature remained stable through verification, and the unit was returned to service.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Disinfection, Rinse, or Drain Cycle Will Not Complete
description: Use this guide when a disinfection, rinse, or drain cycle stalls, aborts, or repeats because of supply, drain, connection, setup, or hydraulic problems.

steps.title: 1. Keep the Machine Out of Clinical Use
steps.instructions: Do not place a dialysis machine into patient service when a required disinfection or rinse process has not completed successfully or when its status is uncertain. If a cycle stops unexpectedly, preserve the displayed status and do not represent the machine as ready for use. Expected outcome: The machine remains unavailable for patient treatment until processing status is verified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Cycle Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure occurred during disinfection, rinse, drain, or another cleaning-related stage. Record where the cycle stopped and any displayed message. Ask whether the problem began after moving the machine, changing a chemical container, or altering the drain or water setup. Expected outcome: The failed stage is clearly identified and documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify Water Supply
steps.instructions: Inspect the external water connection for adequate supply, secure connection, leakage, or kinking. Determine whether other machines using the same supply are affected. Expected outcome: A stable water supply is available. If restoring water supply allows the cycle to complete normally, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Drain Hose and Drain Point
steps.instructions: Check the drain hose for kinks, obstruction, compression, improper elevation, or poor positioning at the drain connection. Ensure the drain location itself is not obviously blocked or backing up. Expected outcome: Drainage is unrestricted. If correcting the drain path resolves the problem, troubleshooting can stop after a successful full cycle.

steps.title: 5. Verify Required Cleaning or Disinfection Supplies
steps.instructions: Confirm any required approved solution is present, correctly connected, and sufficient for the selected process. Inspect pickup tubing and connectors for incomplete insertion, visible air entry, damage, or obstruction. Do not substitute unapproved chemicals. Expected outcome: Required supplies are available and properly connected.

steps.title: 6. Check External Hoses and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible fluid hoses and connectors for leaks, loose fittings, collapsed sections, or incorrect routing that could interrupt filling, circulation, or draining. Expected outcome: External fluid pathways are intact and correctly arranged.

steps.title: 7. Restart the Required Cycle Appropriately
steps.instructions: After correcting an identified external issue, restart the required cycle according to normal facility and manufacturer procedures. Do not skip to clinical use because a partial cycle appeared to complete. Expected outcome: The complete required cycle finishes without alarm or interruption.

steps.title: 8. Verify Completion and Readiness Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine clearly indicates completion of the required process and is left in the appropriate status for subsequent preparation. Check for leaks, residual messages, or abnormal operation. Expected outcome: The complete cycle finishes successfully and the machine meets normal readiness requirements. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the 5008S CorDiax repeatedly stopped before completing the rinse and drain cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the drain hose compressed between the machine and wall, restricting flow.
CCR.Resolution: The drain hose was repositioned, the complete cycle finished normally, and machine readiness was verified before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Results of the completed repeat cycle.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Network, Treatment Record, or Data Export Fails
description: Use this guide when network communication, treatment-record transfer, or data export fails because of cabling, connectivity, configuration, destination, or infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Workflow and Preserve Treatment Information
steps.instructions: Determine whether the communication failure affects active patient care, documentation, treatment review, or another required workflow. Do not interrupt safe dialysis solely to troubleshoot a noncritical network issue. Ensure clinical staff have an approved alternate documentation method if treatment data cannot transfer electronically. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely and required treatment information is not lost because of the communication problem.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine cannot connect to the network, cannot send a treatment record, cannot reach a destination system, fails only on export, or loses communication intermittently. Record any displayed message and the affected destination or workflow. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to network connection, application workflow, or data transfer.

steps.title: 3. Check the Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible network cable and connector for looseness, broken latches, damage, contamination, or disconnection. Reseat the connection where appropriate and inspect the corresponding wall jack or approved network interface. Expected outcome: The physical connection is secure. If communication returns after reseating or replacing a damaged cable, proceed to verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check Link and Network Status
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible communication indicators or network status information without entering unauthorized service menus. If accessible network hardware provides a normal link indication, confirm the connection appears active. Expected outcome: Physical link presence is verified or the problem is localized to the network path.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Cable or Port
steps.instructions: When facility policy permits, test with a known-good network cable or an approved network connection known to support the device. Do not move the machine to an arbitrary jack or VLAN without coordinating with IT. Expected outcome: A defective cable or local port is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Other Devices
steps.instructions: Determine whether other dialysis machines or systems in the same area can communicate normally with the same destination. If multiple devices are failing simultaneously, suspect shared network, server, middleware, or interface infrastructure rather than multiple machine failures. Expected outcome: The issue is localized to the individual machine or escalated as a shared infrastructure event.

steps.title: 7. Verify User-Accessible Configuration
steps.instructions: Compare the machine's approved network or destination configuration with documented values or a known-good equivalent system where authorized. Do not alter IP addressing, destination configuration, certificates, security parameters, or service settings without appropriate approval. Expected outcome: No obvious configuration discrepancy is present, or an authorized correction restores communication.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Receiving System
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended server, treatment-record system, interface, or export destination is available through the appropriate IT or application-support resource. A machine may be functioning correctly while the destination system is unavailable. Expected outcome: The receiving system is confirmed operational or the issue is appropriately reassigned to infrastructure support.

steps.title: 9. Test the Complete Data Path
steps.instructions: After correction, perform an approved nonpatient communication or data-transfer test when available. Verify information reaches the intended destination and is associated with the correct machine or test record. Expected outcome: Data passes through the complete communication path successfully. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify communication remains stable and that no unrelated machine function was affected during troubleshooting. Confirm any temporarily used alternate clinical documentation process can be closed appropriately. Expected outcome: Network and data-transfer functionality are restored and verified end to end.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported treatment records from the 5008S CorDiax were no longer reaching the clinical documentation system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the network cable latch was broken and the connector was intermittently losing link at the machine.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was replaced with a known-good approved cable, a test transfer reached the intended system successfully, and network communication was verified stable.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Use this guide when the system is unresponsive, loses power, or stops during startup after basic external power and connection problems are suspected.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a dialysis machine while a patient depends on unreliable operation. If treatment is underway and the machine loses power, repeatedly restarts, or cannot complete startup, follow the facility's clinical contingency process and move treatment to another verified dialysis machine as appropriate. Inspect for smoke, unusual odor, excessive heat, liquid intrusion, or obvious physical damage. If any are present, disconnect the machine from AC power when safe, label it Out of Service, and stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by safe alternate equipment and the affected machine can be evaluated without clinical dependence. If a clear unsafe condition is identified, troubleshooting stops and the device is removed from service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Ask staff what occurred immediately before the problem and reproduce the condition only when safe. Determine whether the machine is completely dead, powers briefly and shuts down, freezes during startup, restarts repeatedly, or displays a startup message. Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting or clearing it prematurely. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly defined and repeatable enough to guide further checks. If the machine now starts normally and remains stable, continue through final verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully seated and inspect the cord and plug for damage, looseness, discoloration, or overheating. Verify the receptacle has power using an approved tester or known-good load in accordance with facility practice. Avoid extension cords, damaged adapters, or questionable power strips. Expected outcome: A verified AC source is available and the machine receives power through an undamaged connection. If restoring a valid power source corrects the problem and startup completes normally, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check External Power Controls and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the machine's accessible power controls are in the correct operating position and that no externally accessible emergency disconnect or facility power control is preventing startup. Inspect accessible peripheral and communication connections for anything obviously loose, damaged, or improperly connected that could interfere with initialization. Expected outcome: All external power controls and accessible connections are correctly positioned and secure. If correcting an external connection restores normal startup, no further troubleshooting is needed beyond verification.
