steps.title: 5. Allow a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: With the machine disconnected from patient use, perform a normal power-down and restart using approved operating controls. Do not rapidly cycle power or repeatedly restart a machine that shuts itself down. Observe whether startup progresses farther and note exactly where it stops. Expected outcome: The machine completes startup without freezing, restarting, or presenting unresolved startup faults. If it does, continue to functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm ventilation openings are unobstructed and the machine has not recently been exposed to liquid, condensation, unusual heat, or an unstable electrical environment. If the machine was moved, verify no cables, hoses, or accessories were pinched or disturbed during transport. Expected outcome: The operating environment and external setup are suitable for normal startup. Any correctable environmental cause is removed.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Setup
steps.instructions: When practical, compare the machine's external power arrangement and connected accessories with another functioning 5008S CorDiax in the same area. Substitute only approved external accessories when doing so will not alter clinical configuration. Expected outcome: An external accessory or setup difference is either identified and corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After startup completes, verify the machine remains powered, displays and controls respond normally, required self-checks complete, and no new alarms or abnormal behavior appears. Do not return the machine to service solely because it powers on once after an unexplained shutdown or restart. Expected outcome: The machine completes a stable startup and required operational checks without recurrence. If successful, troubleshooting can stop and the device may proceed through normal return-to-service requirements.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the 5008S CorDiax would not complete startup after being moved into the treatment bay.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the AC power cord was not fully seated at the machine and no internal fault was evident after correction.
CCR.Resolution: The power connection was secured, the machine completed startup and operational checks normally, and the device was returned to service after final verification.

title: Fresenius Medical Care 5008S CorDiax Hemodialysis (HD) Machine - Ultrafiltration or Fluid-Balance Test Fails
description: Use this guide when an ultrafiltration or fluid-balance check fails because of connections, fluid supply, leakage, setup, disposables, or hydraulic-system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unverified Fluid Removal
steps.instructions: Do not use a machine for treatment when ultrafiltration or fluid-balance performance cannot be verified. If a failure occurs during treatment, follow the clinical contingency procedure and transfer the patient to another verified machine when appropriate. Expected outcome: The patient is not exposed to an unverified fluid-removal system.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the machine fails a startup fluid-balance check, aborts an ultrafiltration-related test, alarms during treatment preparation, or shows inconsistent fluid-balance behavior. Record the exact displayed condition and the stage at which the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly documented and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Check incoming water, drain, concentrate, dialysate-related hoses, and accessible fluid connections for kinks, leaks, loose fittings, improper routing, or restrictions. Inspect the area around the machine for visible fluid that may indicate an external leak. Expected outcome: External fluid paths are secure, unrestricted, and free of visible leakage.

steps.title: 4. Verify Drain Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm the drain hose is correctly positioned, not kinked, elevated improperly, obstructed, or inserted in a way that prevents normal drainage. Compare the setup with another functioning machine if necessary. Expected outcome: The machine can drain freely. If correcting the drain setup allows the test to pass, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Water and Concentrate Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm adequate external water supply and correct concentrate setup. A poor supply condition can interfere with hydraulic preparation and testing. Check whether other dialysis machines connected to the same infrastructure are experiencing similar problems. Expected outcome: Required external supplies are stable and an infrastructure problem is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Applicable Disposable and Connection Setup
steps.instructions: Verify any required external disposable, connector, or fluid pathway used for the test is installed correctly and is not leaking or obstructed. Do not open internal hydraulic components. Expected outcome: External setup does not explain the test failure.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Test Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue, repeat the normal approved machine test once. Avoid repeated cycling of a test that continues to fail without a new corrective action. Expected outcome: The test completes normally. If it passes consistently after correction, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the machine completes the applicable fluid-balance or ultrafiltration checks and no related alarms, leaks, or abnormal hydraulic behavior recur. Expected outcome: Fluid-management verification completes successfully and the machine is suitable for normal return-to-service processing.

CCR.Complaint: Dialysis staff reported the 5008S CorDiax repeatedly failed its fluid-balance test during preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the drain hose was sharply kinked behind the machine and restricting normal drainage.
CCR.Resolution: The drain hose was repositioned, the fluid-balance test was repeated successfully, and the machine passed final operational verification before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact test or displayed failure message.
